name: Game UI Database
notable: Browse games by platform, genre, theme, aesthetic and camera, with an in-page toolkit for hex-colour search, grid overlays, colour-blind filters and a CRT scanline visualiser.

name: Interface In Game
notable: Screenshot archive browsable by game, genre or screen element (inventory, map, dialogue, game over, loading, lobby) plus interviews with UI designers.

name: gamegui.net Game Interface Archive
notable: Long-running interface archive tagged by genre and by individual title, with separate archive, articles and blog modes.

name: PlayCraft Game UI Gallery
notable: Interface screenshots from 208 games tagged by screen type, pattern, element, colour and art style, each with a written 'What to study' note.

name: PlayCraft Game Tools
notable: Web companion tools for specific games (tech-tree explorer, army builder, planners, patch trackers) that show data-dense interactive UI done in plain web pages.

name: Endless Legend 2 Tech-Tree Explorer
notable: Interactive tech-tree explorer for a strategy game, a ready example of navigating a large dependency graph on the web.
mechanic: The visitor browses a tech tree, causing dependent technologies to be highlighted, which reveals what research path leads to a goal.

name: Endless Legend 2 Army Builder
notable: Web army-composition tool for a strategy game, a configurator pattern with live stat feedback.
mechanic: The visitor assembles units into an army, causing the totals to recompute, which reveals the strengths and gaps of the composition.

name: Endless Legend 2 District Planner
notable: Browser planner for laying out city districts in a strategy game.
mechanic: The visitor places districts in a plan, causing adjacency and output numbers to update, which reveals the best layout.

name: Foundation: Mission List book (PlayCraft)
notable: Missions arrive as a two-page book with the list on the left, briefing and assignable companies on the right, bookmark tabs on top and a single Deploy button carrying the odds.

name: Dune: Awakening event detail (PlayCraft)
notable: Event page with parallel Community and Personal contribution milestone tracks under a 'What do I need to do?' divider, each with its own reward tiers.

name: Indiana Jones and the Great Circle camera viewfinder (PlayCraft)
notable: Photography HUD reduced to a focus frame, a vignette and a three-step 35/50/75 zoom readout, so framing the shot is the whole interface.

name: DOOM: The Dark Ages Atlan mech HUD (PlayCraft)
notable: Third HUD in one trailer and the sparsest: only a compass, a score and the mech's own body, because at mech scale the cockpit frame carries the feedback.

name: Homeworld 3 selected-unit dossier (PlayCraft)
notable: Selecting a capital ship swaps squad cards for a one-ship dossier with a health bar and stance toggle, while an in-frame prompt teaches 'hold right mouse to activate camera'.

name: Soulframe combat HUD (PlayCraft)
notable: A painterly HUD that does not swap chrome for combat; it annotates the exploration frame with nameplate, ability orbs and target reads in the same corners.

name: Slay the Spire interface (Interface In Game)
notable: Catalogued with 14 overlay and 12 in-game captures, including player-turn and attack-enemy states of a card-and-map interface.

name: Hi-Fi Rush interface (Interface In Game)
notable: Rhythm-action game whose interface and combat feedback are built around the beat, a useful study in motion-timed UI.

name: Hades interface (Interface In Game)
notable: Illustrated boon-choice cards and portrait-led dialogue boxes make a repeating menu feel like story.

name: Hollow Knight interface (Interface In Game)
notable: Compact mask-and-soul HUD plus a map that must be bought and drawn in-world, treating navigation UI as part of the fiction.

name: Death Stranding interface (Interface In Game)
notable: Traversal-first interface where weight, balance and route information surface on the character and wrist device rather than in flat overlays.

name: Zachtronics
notable: Studio site for the makers of engineering-puzzle games whose in-game programming interfaces are a recurring reference for puzzle UIs.

name: js13kGames
notable: Yearly JavaScript game competition where the whole entry must fit in a 13 KB zip; current site is for the 2026 edition.

name: js13kGames 2024 winners
notable: 187 entries on the theme Triskaidekaphobia; the top-13 list leads with 13th Floor, Coup Ahoo and Ghosted.

name: js13kGames 2025 winners
notable: 197 entries on the theme Black Cat; the top-13 list leads with CLAWSTRIKE, Cat Survivors and Witchcat.

name: GMTK Game Jam 2024
notable: Jam hosted by Game Maker's Toolkit with 7,511 entries and 158k ratings on the theme 'Built to Scale', with the host's favourites in a results video.

name: GMTK Game Jam 2025
notable: Annual GMTK jam held 2025-07-30 to 2025-08-03, entries browsable and rated on itch.io.

name: Ludum Dare
notable: Long-running solo game jam site with per-event entry galleries, one of the main feeds of experimental browser games.

name: itch.io top-rated Interactive Fiction
notable: Top-rated list for the interactive fiction tag; dominated by visual novels such as Butterfly Soup and Our Life, so it needs filtering for experimental text work.

name: itch.io top-rated Incremental
notable: Top-rated incremental tag list that includes the narrative incremental Trust the System alongside shrimp-boat and plant-growing clickers.

name: itch.io top-rated browser games
notable: Top-rated list of games tagged browser; mixes polished jam entries with small essay-games like Meanderware.

name: Jay Is Games
notable: Review site since 2003 for online, browser and casual games, a long archive of the Flash-era escape and puzzle scene.

name: Universal Paperclips
notable: A clicker whose plain text-and-button interface gradually becomes a console for a runaway paperclip optimiser, with new panels appearing as the stakes escalate.
mechanic: The visitor makes paperclips and tunes price and production, causing new panels, projects and scales to unlock, which reveals an AI maximiser consuming everything.

name: A Dark Room
notable: A minimalist text adventure that begins as a single 'light the fire' button and adds tabs for the village, world and ship as you progress.
mechanic: The visitor stokes a fire and gathers wood, causing villagers and new menu tabs to appear, which reveals a larger world and story hidden behind a one-button start.

name: The Password Game
notable: A single password field that keeps adding absurd rules, using a form as a pressure cooker.
mechanic: The visitor types a password, causing a growing list of rules to appear and re-check on every keystroke, which reveals increasingly absurd constraints.

name: Wordle
notable: Six guesses at a hidden word with coloured tile feedback and a spoiler-free emoji share grid; the model for the daily-puzzle format.
mechanic: The visitor guesses five-letter words, causing tiles to flip green, yellow or grey, which reveals the hidden word through elimination.

name: Absurdle
notable: A Wordle variant in which the game is adversarial and avoids committing to an answer for as long as it can.
mechanic: The visitor guesses words, causing the game to pick whichever feedback keeps the most candidate words alive, which reveals how an answer can be narrowed from an adversary.

name: Redactle
notable: An entire Wikipedia article blacked out, uncovered one guessed word at a time until you can name the title.
mechanic: The visitor guesses words, causing matching black bars across the article to open, which reveals the text and eventually the article title.

name: Worldle
notable: Daily geography game that shows a country's silhouette and adds direction and distance clues with each guess.
mechanic: The visitor guesses a country from its shape, causing distance and compass feedback to appear, which reveals the answer by triangulation.

name: Semantle
notable: Word-guessing game scored by semantic similarity rather than spelling, so wrong guesses still carry information.
mechanic: The visitor enters words, causing a similarity score to be shown against the secret word, which reveals the meaning neighbourhood of the answer.

name: Contexto
notable: Guess the secret word with an AI telling you how close each guess ranks.
mechanic: The visitor types guesses, causing each word to be ranked by closeness in a growing list, which reveals the secret word's semantic context.

name: Nerdle
notable: A Wordle-style daily game where the guesses are valid equations, with classic, mini, speed and pro modes.
mechanic: The visitor enters equations, causing tiles to colour by position and value, which reveals the hidden calculation.

name: Globle
notable: Geography guessing played on a 3D globe where each guess is coloured by how close it is.
mechanic: The visitor guesses countries, causing them to colour on a rotating globe from cool to hot, which reveals where the target country lies.

name: Increasingly Cursed Wordle Puzzles
notable: Wordle with extra colours whose meaning you must deduce rather than being told.
mechanic: The visitor makes guesses, causing tiles to turn unfamiliar colours, which reveals the unstated rules that those colours encode.

name: Cipher (BenColeWu)
notable: Puzzle game pitched as solving glyphs without a manual, so the interface teaches itself through experiment.
mechanic: The visitor tries glyph combinations, causing the game to respond, which reveals the hidden rules of the symbol system.

name: Trust the System
notable: A narrative incremental about stamping papers at a desk until you leave it.
mechanic: The visitor stamps papers over and over, causing upgrades and story beats to unlock, which reveals a way to leave the desk.

name: Meanderware: Things I loved about cyberspace
notable: A short playable essay and poetic breadcrumb trail of thoughts about cyberspace and the internet.
mechanic: The visitor wanders through the piece, causing fragments about early internet experiences to surface, which reveals the author's essay on cyberspace.

name: Clam Man 2: Open Mic
notable: A combatless RPG where jokes are loot and boss fights are comedy sets.
mechanic: The visitor collects and picks jokes, causing the audience to react in a stand-up set, which reveals whether the routine wins the room.

name: A Quiet Winter Walk Home
notable: A short ambient walk home from a train station in winter.
mechanic: The visitor walks forward along the route, causing the winter scene to unfold, which reveals a quiet slice of an evening commute.

name: Inktober 2020 Demo Disc
notable: An interactive 3D gallery of an artist's Inktober pieces styled as a PS1 demo disc, a portfolio disguised as a retro game.
mechanic: The visitor moves through a PS1-style demo disc menu and 3D rooms, causing artwork to be presented as game content, which reveals the artist's portfolio.

name: The Final Earth 2
notable: A browser colony builder where you grow a futuristic space settlement.
mechanic: The visitor places buildings on a planet, causing resources and population to grow, which reveals larger colony tiers.

name: Idle Breakout
notable: Idle game that turns brick-breaking into an upgrade tree of different balls.
mechanic: The visitor buys and upgrades balls, causing bricks to break automatically, which reveals stronger ball types and higher levels.

name: Cookie Clicker
notable: The archetypal idle game where you click a cookie and deal with deranged grandmothers, with news tickers and achievements as its voice.
mechanic: The visitor clicks a cookie and buys helpers, causing production to compound and strange new upgrades to appear, which reveals a darker grandma-driven storyline.

name: Nested
notable: A universe-expanding game where you land on procedural planets and read the thoughts of living things; Orteil's own favourite work.
mechanic: The visitor zooms into a procedural universe, causing galaxies, planets and creatures to be generated at deeper scales, which reveals ever more nested worlds.

name: NeverEnding Legacy
notable: Half-idle, half-strategy game that leads a people from starving cavemen to a thriving civilisation.
mechanic: The visitor assigns people to tasks and researches, causing the tribe to grow and new eras to open, which reveals the arc of a civilisation.

name: Murder Games
notable: Automated survival simulator in which you build a cast and watch them betray each other round by round.
mechanic: The visitor creates a cast of characters, causing them to scheme and eliminate each other round by round, which reveals the last survivor.

name: RandomGen
notable: A tool for writing and sharing random generators in a simple syntax, with community-made generators.
mechanic: The visitor writes a template in a simple syntax, causing random results to be generated on each press, which reveals the variety of the generator.

name: Idle Game Maker
notable: Lets you build your own idle game just by writing a text file, with extensive docs.
mechanic: The visitor edits a text definition, causing an idle game to be generated from it, which reveals the mechanics of idle games.

name: Tea Party
notable: A mindless, meandering text adventure full of dead ends.
mechanic: The visitor picks text choices, causing the story to wander and often dead-end, which reveals a surreal tea-party world.

name: PretendEverything
notable: Any experience can be reduced to one line of text and a couple of buttons.
mechanic: The visitor presses one of a couple of buttons beneath a line of text, causing the next line to replace it, which reveals a tiny whole experience.

name: Dreamlog
notable: A little adventure made from a real dream, featuring rabbits, fishing and strange museums.
mechanic: The visitor moves through the dream's scenes, causing events to play out, which reveals a strange museum and fishing world.

name: Kittens Game
notable: Billed as a Dark Souls of incremental gaming; a text-and-tabs civilisation sim run through a kitten village.
mechanic: The visitor gathers catnip and assigns kittens to jobs, causing new resources and tabs to open, which reveals a deep civilisation tree.

name: Candy Box 2
notable: ASCII-art adventure that starts from a candy counter and grows into a sprawling mix of quests, maps and mini-games.
mechanic: The visitor collects candy and buys items, causing new ASCII areas and mechanics to open, which reveals a larger adventure.

name: Candy Box!
notable: The original ASCII candy-counting game that reveals new interface elements as the candy count rises.
mechanic: The visitor waits for and spends candies, causing new ASCII features to appear, which reveals a hidden game under a counter.

name: Antimatter Dimensions
notable: Incremental game of buying dimensions whose numbers escalate through layered prestige resets.
mechanic: The visitor buys dimensions and resets, causing multipliers to compound, which reveals deeper prestige layers.

name: Progress Knight
notable: Life-progress incremental where you train skills, take jobs and rebirth for bonuses.
mechanic: The visitor switches jobs and skills, causing time and XP to flow, which reveals higher careers after rebirth.

name: Evolve
notable: A very dense incremental UI that takes a species from primordial ooze to a star-faring civilisation.
mechanic: The visitor allocates resources and researches, causing a species to evolve through eras, which reveals the next tier of the tech tree.

name: Little Alchemy 2
notable: Mix items to create the world from scratch, with funny descriptions for each discovered item.
mechanic: The visitor drags two elements together, causing a new item to appear, which reveals a library of combinations.

name: Infinite Craft
notable: A crafting game where you can make anything; two dragged-together items yield an AI-generated result.
mechanic: The visitor drops two elements onto each other, causing a new generated element to appear, which reveals an effectively infinite combination space.

notable: Join tiles to reach 2048; swipe and arrow-key sliding on a 4x4 grid became a viral pattern.
mechanic: The visitor slides the grid, causing equal tiles to merge, which reveals higher numbers until 2048.

name: Bennett Foddy: QWOP
notable: A sprinting game where four keys control a runner's thighs and calves, making deliberately hard controls the joke.
mechanic: The visitor presses Q, W, O and P, causing a sprinter's thighs and calves to move, which reveals how hard it is to run 100 metres.

name: Bennett Foddy: GIRP
notable: A keyboard-driven climbing game from Bennett Foddy.
mechanic: The visitor presses keys to grip and reach, causing a climber to move up a wall, which reveals whether the route can be completed.

name: Bennett Foddy: CLOP
notable: A follow-up to QWOP built on a four-key control scheme for an animal.
mechanic: The visitor presses four keys to move the legs, causing a creature to lurch forward, which reveals the difficulty of a simple stride.

name: Bennett Foddy: Getting Over It
notable: A mouse-driven mountain-climbing game where a hammer is the only tool and a narrator comments on your failures; PC release, not browser.
mechanic: The visitor swings a hammer with the mouse, causing a man in a pot to climb or fall, which reveals the mountain and the narrator's commentary.

name: Bennett Foddy: Baby Steps
notable: Latest game announced on Foddy's site (Feb 2026 post); a PC title about difficult walking controls, not browser-playable.
mechanic: The visitor controls a character's steps one leg at a time, causing awkward progress across terrain, which reveals the game's mountain.

name: The Evolution of Trust
notable: An interactive guide to the game theory of why and how we trust each other, built as a playable sequence of small simulations.
mechanic: The visitor plays repeated trust games and adjusts rules and noise, causing populations of strategies to shift, which reveals when trust evolves or collapses.

name: Parable of the Polygons
notable: A playable post on how harmless choices can make a harmful world, using shapes that move when unhappy.
mechanic: The visitor drags unhappy shapes and tweaks how much they want like neighbours, causing the board to cluster or mix, which reveals how mild bias produces segregation.

name: Adventures With Anxiety!
notable: A story-game in which you play as a person's anxiety.
mechanic: The visitor plays the anxiety and chooses what to whisper, causing the human's reactions to change, which reveals how anxiety works from the inside.

name: The Wisdom and/or Madness of Crowds
notable: An interactive guide to human networks, from spread to polarisation.
mechanic: The visitor plays with network connections and thresholds, causing ideas or behaviours to spread, which reveals why crowds turn wise or mad.

name: LOOPY
notable: A tool for thinking in systems where you draw circles and arrows and then watch the loop run.
mechanic: The visitor draws nodes and arrows, causing signals to propagate around the loop, which reveals the feedback dynamics of the system.

name: Fireflies
notable: A small, serene simulation of self-synchronisation among fireflies.
mechanic: The visitor observes and nudges the swarm, causing flashes to influence each other, which reveals synchronisation emerging.

name: To Build a Better Ballot
notable: An interactive guide to alternative voting systems with live example elections.
mechanic: The visitor casts ballots under different voting rules, causing the winner to change, which reveals how the method shapes the outcome.

name: We Become What We Behold
notable: A short game about news cycles, vicious cycles and infinite cycles.
mechanic: The visitor frames events as a news camera, causing coverage to escalate the stories shown, which reveals a vicious media feedback loop.

name: Coming Out Simulator 2014
notable: A half-true story about half-truths, told through dialogue choices.
mechanic: The visitor picks what to say in a conversation, causing the story to branch, which reveals what was hidden and why.

name: I Am Become Anime
notable: A webcam toy made for the 2018 Stupid Sh*t Nobody Needs hackathon.
mechanic: The visitor poses in front of a webcam, causing the image to be transformed in the browser, which reveals an anime-styled version of themselves.

name: Nutshell
notable: A tool to make expandable explanations where a phrase opens into more text inline.
mechanic: The visitor clicks an underlined phrase, causing a deeper explanation to expand in place, which reveals extra context without leaving the page.

name: Emoji Simulator
notable: A tool to make cellular automata with emoji.
mechanic: The visitor defines rules for emoji, causing a grid to evolve, which reveals emergent patterns.

name: Explorable Explanations (hub)
notable: A hub for learning through play, collecting explorable explanations from many authors.

name: How to Remember Anything Forever-ish
notable: An interactive comic on the science of memory that quizzes you as you read.
mechanic: The visitor answers recall prompts while reading, causing the comic to space out repeats, which reveals how spaced repetition works.

name: The Double Slit Simulation
notable: A tiny explanation-free simulation made in two days for a friend.
mechanic: The visitor changes the setup, causing the interference pattern to redraw, which reveals wave behaviour.

name: Stimulation Clicker
notable: A satirical clicker about escalating stimulation and short attention spans.
mechanic: The visitor clicks to gain stimulation, causing more screens and distractions to pile up, which reveals the absurdity of constant attention-feeding.

name: Absurd Trolley Problems
notable: A string of increasingly silly trolley-problem set-ups with a final tally comparing your choices to others.
mechanic: The visitor chooses which track the trolley takes, causing a funny outcome to play out, which reveals how their choices compare to everyone else's.

name: Internet Roadtrip
notable: A shared road trip through Street View where the whole internet steers the same car.
mechanic: The visitor votes on where to turn, causing one shared Street View journey to move on, which reveals the places a crowd drives to.

name: Draw a Perfect Circle
notable: Draw a circle freehand and get a numeric roundness score.
mechanic: The visitor draws a circle with the mouse, causing a score to be computed, which reveals how close to perfect it is.

name: Not a Robot
notable: A CAPTCHA parody whose tests escalate into absurdity.
mechanic: The visitor passes proof-of-humanity tests, causing the tests to get weirder, which reveals how arbitrary such checks can be.

name: Cursor Camp
notable: A shared space where visitors' cursors meet around a camp.
mechanic: The visitor moves their cursor, causing it to appear to other visitors in a shared scene, which reveals a crowd of other people.

name: The Deep Sea
notable: A scroll-driven descent into the ocean where creatures appear at their real depths.
mechanic: The visitor scrolls down, causing the screen to darken and deeper creatures to pass by with depth labels, which reveals how deep the ocean goes.

name: The Size of Space
notable: A scrolling comparison of cosmic object sizes.
mechanic: The visitor scrolls through objects of growing size, causing each to be compared to the last, which reveals the scale of the universe.

name: Spend Bill Gates' Money
notable: A shopping interface for spending a vast fortune that shows how little you can dent it.
mechanic: The visitor buys items, causing a receipt to grow and the remaining balance to barely move, which reveals how huge the fortune is.

name: Wonders of Street View
notable: A curated tour of landmark views from Street View.
mechanic: The visitor steps through selected views, causing each wonder to be shown with context, which reveals places they might not have found.

name: Rocks (neal.fun)
notable: A peaceful rock stacking game.
mechanic: The visitor stacks rocks, causing a balanced pile to grow, which reveals how high the stack can go.

name: Asteroid Launcher
notable: A sandbox for choosing an asteroid and hitting Earth with it.
mechanic: The visitor picks an asteroid and a target, causing an impact to be simulated, which reveals the scale of damage.

name: Logos From Memory
notable: A drawing challenge where you recreate famous logos from memory and see them next to the real ones.
mechanic: The visitor draws a logo from memory, causing it to be compared to the real one, which reveals how little we remember of familiar brands.

name: Life Stats
notable: Turns a birthday into live counters of heartbeats, breaths and similar life statistics.
mechanic: The visitor enters a birth date, causing live counters to start running, which reveals how many things a life has already done.

name: neal.fun
notable: Neal Agarwal's front page of web toys, each a single-idea interaction, with a 'watered 0 times today' plant on the homepage.

name: Quick, Draw!
notable: A neural network tries to recognise your doodles under a timer while the data helps teach it.
mechanic: The visitor sketches a prompted object against the clock, causing the network to guess live, which reveals how well it recognises doodles.

name: Spent
notable: Interactive game that makes you manage money, raise a child and make hard choices on a poverty budget.
mechanic: The visitor makes money decisions across a month, causing the balance and options to shrink, which reveals the constraints of poverty.

name: Pointer Pointer
notable: Shows a photo of a person pointing at exactly where your cursor is.
mechanic: The visitor moves the cursor, causing a matching photo of someone pointing at it to appear, which reveals a huge database of pointing photos.

name: The Wiki Game
notable: Race through Wikipedia links from a start article to a target.
mechanic: The visitor clicks article links, causing the path to extend, which reveals a route from one topic to another.

name: Hacker Typer
notable: Pseudo-hacking toy: any keys you hit produce code on screen.
mechanic: The visitor mashes the keyboard, causing realistic code to scroll out, which reveals them 'hacking'.

name: Agar.io
notable: Control a cell with the mouse, eat smaller ones and avoid bigger ones in a single shared arena.
mechanic: The visitor steers a cell with the cursor, causing it to absorb smaller cells and grow, which reveals who dominates the arena.

name: slither.io
notable: A massively multiplayer snake game where the longest snake of the day leads.
mechanic: The visitor steers a snake toward food, causing it to grow longer, which reveals a leaderboard of the longest.

name: HexGL
notable: A futuristic racing game built with HTML5, JavaScript and WebGL by one developer.
mechanic: The visitor steers a hovercraft around a track, causing speed and lap time to change, which reveals how far browser 3D could go.

name: Google Pac-Man doodle
notable: A playable Pac-Man doodle shown in place of the Google logo.
mechanic: The visitor steers Pac-Man in the logo, causing ghosts and dots to react, which reveals a full arcade game in place of a logo.

name: Google Doodles archive
notable: Archive of logo changes over the years, including many interactive and game doodles.

name: A Short Hike (browser)
notable: A little exploration game about hiking up a mountain, a model of tiny cozy scope.
mechanic: The visitor hikes toward a summit, causing the island to open up with people and tasks, which reveals the mountain top.

name: Celeste Classic
notable: The PICO-8 original of Celeste ('climb a mountain') playable on itch.
mechanic: The visitor jumps and dashes up a mountain, causing screens to change, which reveals a summit at the top.

name: PICO-8
notable: Fantasy console for making and sharing tiny games, with carts playable in the browser.

name: Rusty Lake
notable: Studio of surreal point-and-click escape games with a site that presents the games as a world.
mechanic: The visitor clicks through rooms, causing objects to be combined, which reveals the next surreal scene.

name: Samorost 1
notable: The short puzzle adventure that launched Amanita Design, a hand-built illustrated world playable in-page.
mechanic: The visitor clicks on parts of an illustrated scene, causing things to move and chain together, which reveals the next scene.

name: A Slower Speed of Light
notable: MIT Game Lab game that visualises relativistic effects by lowering the speed of light.
mechanic: The visitor collects orbs, causing the speed of light to drop, which reveals relativistic distortions of sight.

name: Bitsy
notable: A little engine for little games, worlds and stories with an in-browser editor.
mechanic: The visitor paints a room and places items and dialogue, causing a playable tiny world to appear, which reveals a story.

name: PuzzleScript
notable: Open-source HTML5 puzzle engine where the whole game is defined by a rule text; many Increpare games use it.
mechanic: The visitor writes rewrite rules in text, causing a Sokoban-like puzzle to run, which reveals the game from its rules.

name: Flickgame
notable: Draw and share simple games with your mouse or fingers.
mechanic: The visitor draws scenes and links regions between them, causing a click-through game to form, which reveals a story or puzzle.

name: increpare games
notable: Stephen Lavelle's catalogue with play-now HTML5 and source links per game, including games built in PuzzleScript and flickgame.

name: Vectorpark
notable: Interactive art and games by Patrick Smith, creator of Windosill, Metamorphabet, Feed the Head, Levers and more.
mechanic: The visitor pokes and drags illustrated objects, causing them to transform in surprising ways, which reveals playful hidden behaviours.

name: Net Art Anthology
notable: Rhizome's collection of restored and emulated net art, each work presented with context and a running or emulated copy.

name: Simple Net Art Diagram
notable: A bare diagram of two computers joined by a lightning bolt labelled 'the art happens here', still one of the shortest statements of what net art is.
mechanic: The visitor looks at a minimal schematic, causing a joke about where art lives to land, which reveals that the network is the artwork.

name: Vote-Auction
notable: A website that let U.S. voters auction their votes to the highest bidder during the 2000 election, causing a legal firestorm.
mechanic: The visitor lists or bids on a vote, causing a market for ballots to appear on screen, which reveals how an election could be commodified.

name: The Web Stalker
notable: An artist-made browser that challenged commercial conventions by showing a page's structure rather than rendering it.
mechanic: The visitor enters a URL, causing the page to be drawn as nodes, links and raw text instead of the usual layout, which reveals the web's hidden structure.

name: The File Room
notable: A participatory online archive of cases of censorship, extended by submissions from visitors.
mechanic: The visitor browses and adds cases, causing the archive to grow, which reveals a world map of censorship.

name: FloodNET
notable: A virtual sit-in tool from Electronic Disturbance Theater that repeatedly reloaded targeted sites.
mechanic: The visitor joins a protest page, causing repeated page requests to hit a target site, which reveals a collective online action.

name: MOUCHETTE (Rhizome)
notable: Net art persona who invites visitors into unsettling and intimate interactive pages.
mechanic: The visitor clicks through the site, causing eerie interactive pages to open, which reveals the persona's world.

name: Form Art
notable: Art made entirely from HTML form controls such as checkboxes, buttons and fields.
mechanic: The visitor ticks and edits form controls, causing the composition to change, which reveals that default widgets can be material.

name: My Boyfriend Came Back From the War (Rhizome)
notable: Olia Lialina's hypertext story that splits the browser window into ever smaller frames as you click.
mechanic: The visitor clicks fragments of text and image, causing the window to subdivide into more frames, which reveals a fractured conversation.

name: Life Sharing
notable: For three years the artists made the full contents of their home computer publicly accessible.
mechanic: The visitor browses the artists' files, causing a private computer to be exposed, which reveals an entire digital life.

name: Velvet-Strike
notable: A Counter-Strike mod adding anti-war protest sprays to the game's graffiti function.
mechanic: The visitor sprays protest graffiti in the game world, causing a political message to appear in a shooter, which reveals the game as a protest space.

name: Screenfull
notable: A loud, crowded Blogger-hosted blog by Abe Linkoln and Jimpunk taking a maximalist approach to content and design.
mechanic: The visitor scrolls the blog, causing dense stacks of web imagery to fill the screen, which reveals a maximalist web aesthetic.

name: Domestic Tension
notable: Online visitors could remotely fire a paintball gun at the artist during a gallery residency.

name: Refresh

name: Versions

name: EverythingIveEverWantedToKnow.com

name: Heritage Gold

name: Scrubbing Calculator
notable: A prototype calculator in which dragging a number shows how the answer changes.
mechanic: The visitor scrubs a value in an expression, causing the result to update live, which reveals how the answer depends on the input.

name: Explorable Explanations (Bret Victor)
notable: The essay that named explorable explanations as active reading with manipulable models.
mechanic: The visitor manipulates the model embedded in the text, causing the nearby prose and graphics to respond, which reveals the argument by experience.

name: Learnable Programming
notable: An essay and set of mockups on making programming environments show what the code does as you write it.
mechanic: The visitor changes code in the mockups, causing the program's state to be visible immediately, which reveals how an environment can teach.

name: Media for Thinking the Unthinkable
notable: A talk and notes on building tools that make concepts visible and manipulable.

name: Kill Math
notable: Project notes on replacing symbol-heavy maths with interactive and visual representations.

name: Our Choice
notable: Bret Victor's page for Al Gore's multi-touch interactive book on climate solutions.
mechanic: The visitor pinches, taps and blows on the screen, causing visuals and text to change, which reveals data and ideas through touch.

name: Magic Ink
notable: Long essay that argues information software should be designed like graphic design rather than as interactive.

name: Alligator Eggs!
notable: A game that teaches lambda calculus with alligator-eating-eggs rules.
mechanic: The visitor moves hungry alligators over eggs, causing them to eat and hatch, which reveals how lambda calculus evaluates.

name: Visualizing Weights of Graph Edges
notable: A small interactive demo of visualising edge weights in a graph.
mechanic: The visitor drags edge weights, causing the visual to change, which reveals the structure of the graph.

name: A Brief Rant on the Future of Interaction Design
notable: Essay arguing that touchscreen 'pictures under glass' ignore the richness of hands, with a responses page.

name: Scientific Communication as Sequential Art
notable: Essay on using comics-like layouts for scientific papers and explanations.

name: Dynamicland
notable: Bret Victor's community lab for a computer you can work in with paper and walls rather than a screen.
mechanic: The visitor moves paper programs and objects on tables, causing a projected system to react, which reveals computation embedded in space.

name: Seeing Spaces
notable: Talk and poster on a room that makes hardware and invisible phenomena visible.

name: Stop Drawing Dead Fish (talk)
notable: Talk arguing creative tools should let artists build dynamic, behaving drawings rather than static images.

name: Inventing on Principle (talk)
notable: Talk demonstrating live-coding environments in which edits show their effects instantly.

name: Bartosz Ciechanowski
notable: Interactive articles about science and engineering with custom 3D simulations embedded in long essays.
mechanic: The visitor drags handles and sliders inside figures, causing simulations to update, which reveals how mechanisms work.

name: Explained Visually
notable: Collection of interactive visual explanations of mathematical and statistical ideas.
mechanic: The visitor tweaks sliders in visualisations, causing outputs to update, which reveals why the idea works.

name: Red Blob Games
notable: Interactive tutorials for maths and algorithms with live diagrams.
mechanic: The visitor drags points in diagrams, causing the algorithm's output to redraw, which reveals how it behaves.

name: Seeing Theory
notable: A visual introduction to probability and statistics.
mechanic: The visitor runs trials and adjusts parameters, causing distributions to form, which reveals probabilistic behaviour.

name: Visualizing Quaternions
notable: Explains quaternions in 3D rotation with interactive visuals.
mechanic: The visitor drags 3D objects, causing quaternion rotations to be shown, which reveals how 4D numbers describe rotation.

name: Mathigon
notable: The mathematical playground with interactive textbooks.
mechanic: The visitor manipulates diagrams and answers prompts, causing explanations to adapt, which reveals the concept.

name: XXIIVV
notable: A personal wiki and library of tools, projects and notes with a webring.

name: XXIIVV Webring
notable: A webring linking independent personal sites.
mechanic: The visitor follows ring links, causing the next member site to open, which reveals the indie web.

name: Hundred Rabbits
notable: Software studio aboard a sailboat whose site documents its tools and projects.

name: Exhibit of Sorrows
notable: Top-rated HTML5 game about seemingly friendly dolls and a not-so-friendly clown, set in an exhibit.
mechanic: The visitor explores an exhibit and interacts with dolls, causing the mood to turn threatening, which reveals the clown.
